title: Make someone laugh
goal: Make causative verbs with -dyr and -t, and use the common ones that have their own shape.

intro.text: A causative verb is for making someone do something: *gülmek* (to laugh) → *güldürmek* (to make laugh). After a consonant add `-dYr`; after a vowel, *-t*: *okamak* → *okatmak* (to teach). Some verbs have a shape of their own: *turmak* → *turuzmak* (to wake someone up).

vocab.en: to cut (kesdirmek: to have something cut)
baby (bäbegi: the baby, as an object)
to put to bed; to lay down
to wake (someone) up; to get (someone) up

exercises.question: How do you say **to make (someone) laugh**?

why.1: *-t* comes after a vowel. *Gül-* ends in a consonant, so the causative is `-dYr`.
why.2: After *ü* in the first syllable, the vowel of the suffix rounds: *güldür-*.
why.3: Only a few verbs take *-yr*, *-ür*, and *gülmek* isn't one of them: *güldürmek*.

exercises.explain: *gül-* ends in a consonant: `-dYr`, rounded after *ü*: *güldürmek*.
*kes-* ends in a consonant: *-dir*, then the past *-di* and *-m* for **I**.

reject.why: After a vowel the causative is *-t*, here *d*: *okadýar*.
*Güldi* is **laughed**. Making someone laugh is the causative: *güldürdi*.

exercises.explain: *gül-* + *-dür* + *-di*; the one made to laugh is the object: *meni*.

accept: My mother woke me up at seven.
My mother woke me up at [7|seven o'clock|7 o'clock]
My mother got me up at [seven|7]( o'clock)

exercises.label: *okatmak* (to teach), present: I teach, you teach…
exercises.explain: *okat-* + *-ýar*: the *t* becomes *d* before *-ýar*. The endings are those of the present.

exercises.question: Which is **she taught** (past)?

why.1: The *t* turns into *d* only before a vowel or *-ýar*. Before *-dy* it stays: *okatdy*.

exercises.explain: Before a consonant the causative *t* stays: *okatdy*, *okatjak*, *okatmaly*.

reject.why: *Garaşdym* is **I waited**. Keeping someone waiting is the causative: *garaşdyrdym*.

exercises.explain: *garaş-* + *-dyr*: to make wait. The one kept waiting is the object: *sizi*.

exercises.prompt: The mother put the baby to bed.

accept: My father took me to school.
My dad took me to school

exercises.question: *Getirmek* is **to bring**, literally to make come. Which verb is **to take away**, to make go?

why.1: For **take away**, Turkmen uses its own verb: *äkitmek*.

exercises.explain: *Çaýy getir!* Bring the tea. *Bu stakany äkit!* Take this glass away.

accept: [Ertir maňa muny|Maňa ertir muny|Ertir muny maňa] ýatladyň!

reject.why: With *ýatlatmak*, the person reminded takes the dative: *maňa*.
*Ýatla* is **remember**. To remind someone is the causative: *ýatlat*.

exercises.explain: *ýatla-* (remember) + *-t*: make remember, remind. The polite form is *ýatladyň*, with *d* before the vowel.
